title: Between two roaring worlds
html_source:
The two roaring worlds that swirl on either side are of the church in Rome, and of the government in England symbolized respectively by Father Conmee at the beginning of the chapter, and the Viceroy at its end. There are also the worlds of the East and the West, and of the Hebrews and the Greeks, all of which are roundly discussed in Ulysses. Blake T. Ostler in For on the Horizons, writes,

There is a vast difference in the way the Hebrews felt we come to knowledge and the way the Greeks thought of it. Whereas the Hebrews… constantly refer to the heart as an instrument of knowledge and choice, the [Greeks] hardly ever do. The [Hebrews] regard the heart as the source of knowledge and authentic being. For the Greeks, the head is the place of knowing everything we can know.

anchor.prefix: of dynamos from the powerhouse urged Stephen to be on. Beingless beings. Stop! Throb always without you and the throb always within. Your heart you sing of. I between them. Where?
anchor.suffix: where they swirl, I. Shatter them, one and both. But stun myself too in the blow. Shatter me you who can. Bawd and butcher were the words. I say! Not yet awhile. A look around.
